hunks.baseline: Four fine horses raced down the main road. Exhausted from their lack of rest, the horses were already gasping for breath, but there was no way we could loosen the reins.
hunks.sol: Four fine horses thundered down the main road. Exhausted from too little rest, they were already gasping for breath, but we couldn’t afford to slow down.

hunks.baseline: 31, 30. The time kept ticking down.
hunks.sol: Thirty-one, thirty. The seconds kept ticking away.

hunks.baseline: Three *sijin*—six hours—had already passed. We had tried to stop at a small village along the way and find fresh horses, but all they had were small, painfully slow packhorses.
hunks.sol: Three *shichen*—a full six hours—had already passed. We had stopped at a small village along the way to look for fresh horses, but all they had were small, painfully slow packhorses.

hunks.baseline: We had been forcing our march as hard as we could, but the time limit was dangerously close. If we kept running like this, the horses wouldn’t hold out.
hunks.sol: We were already pushing as hard as we could, yet the time limit was still cutting it close. If we kept up this pace, the horses wouldn’t last.

hunks.baseline: *Can’t be helped.*
hunks.sol: *Do we have a choice?*

hunks.baseline: I was just about to suggest to Wolhwa and Jin Mukyung that we rest, even if only briefly, when—
hunks.sol: I was just about to suggest to Wolhwa and Jin Mukyung that we stop, even if only briefly, when—

hunks.baseline: Every one of them wore filthy clothes, with a single curved saber sticking out from his belt. There was no need to say anything more.
hunks.sol: Every one of them wore filthy clothes, with a curved saber jutting from his belt. There was no need to ask who they were.

hunks.baseline: The men had surrounded what appeared to be ordinary civilians and were threatening them. At the sound of hoofbeats, they whipped their heads around.
hunks.sol: They had surrounded a group of what looked like ordinary civilians and were threatening them. At the sound of hoofbeats, they whipped their heads around.

hunks.baseline: The mounted bandits spotted me riding well out in front and grinned, baring their yellow teeth.
hunks.sol: The mounted bandits spotted me riding well ahead of the others and grinned, baring yellow teeth.

hunks.baseline: “Well, look at that. Our next customers have already arrived. Stop!”
hunks.sol: “Well, look at that. Our next customer’s here already. Stop!”

hunks.baseline: The fine horse I was riding didn’t come to a stop until it had trampled the two men blocking the road. The mounted bandits—and even the travelers they had been holding captive—stared at me with their eyes wide.
hunks.sol: My horse didn’t come to a halt until it had trampled the two men blocking the road. The mounted bandits—and even the travelers they had captured—stared at me wide-eyed.

hunks.baseline: I hopped down from the saddle and asked,
“I’m asking just to make sure. You’re the Red Wind Band, right?”
hunks.sol: I hopped down from the saddle and asked, “Just making sure. You’re with the Red Wind Band, right?”

hunks.baseline: “What the hell are you?”
hunks.sol: “Who the hell are you?”

hunks.baseline: “Judging by your reaction, I guess I was right. I’m short on time, so let’s finish this quickly.”
hunks.sol: “Judging by that reaction, I guess you are. I’m short on time, so let’s finish this quickly.”

hunks.baseline: Without hesitation, I kicked the leg of the nearest man.
hunks.sol: Without hesitation, I kicked the nearest man in the leg.

hunks.baseline: With a chilling sound, his shinbone snapped, and he collapsed.
hunks.sol: His shinbone snapped with a sickening crunch, and he crumpled to the ground.

hunks.baseline: It all happened in an instant. The men who had been momentarily stunned quickly thrust curved sabers and spears at me.
hunks.sol: It all happened in an instant. The others stood stunned for a moment, then hastily leveled their curved sabers and spears at me.

hunks.baseline: “A man should always watch his rear.”
hunks.sol: “A man should always watch his back.”

hunks.baseline: “Be careful behind you.”
hunks.sol: “I said, watch behind you.”

hunks.baseline: Three fine horses charging at full speed swept the men away.
hunks.sol: Three fine horses charging at full speed swept them away.

hunks.baseline: The battle was over before it had even begun. The men struck by the horses had been sent flying like bowling pins and lay sprawled out half-dead. The rest were easily subdued.
hunks.sol: The battle was over before it had even begun. The men struck by the horses had gone flying like bowling pins and lay sprawled on the ground, half-dead. The rest were subdued with ease.

hunks.baseline: “P-Please, just spare my life.”
hunks.sol: “P-Please, spare my life.”

hunks.baseline: While Jin Mukyung methodically broke the limbs of the surviving bandits, Hyuk Mujin brought over the horses tied up beside the road.
hunks.sol: While Jin Mukyung methodically snapped the surviving bandits’ limbs, Hyuk Mujin brought over the horses tied beside the road.

hunks.baseline: “It looks like we can switch to these healthy ones. There must be at least ten of them, so we could take them all and switch whenever they get tired.”
hunks.sol: “We can switch to these healthy ones. There are about ten, so we might as well take them all and change horses whenever one gets tired.”

hunks.baseline: I had been thinking the same thing. Unlike the last group we encountered, these mounted bandits each had their own horses. It was fortunate.
hunks.sol: I had been thinking the same thing. Unlike the last group we had encountered, these mounted bandits each had their own horse. That was fortunate.

hunks.baseline: *But still…*
hunks.sol: *Still…*

hunks.sol: According to the information we had obtained at the shrine, more than a hundred remnants had scattered throughout northern Shanxi.

hunks.sol: Some hid in the foothills, others in remote villages or crowded towns, waiting for orders to assemble at the designated rendezvous point.

hunks.sol: They were reserve forces carrying out an operation. The Red Wind Band Leader was replenishing his forces on the plateau and moving south while ordering the subordinates he had left behind to move north.

hunks.baseline: I could easily understand why Wolhwa had described the Red Wind Band Leader as such a terrifying man.
hunks.sol: It wasn’t hard to see why Wolhwa had called him a dangerous man.

hunks.sol: *The judgment to retreat swiftly when the tide turned against him. The foresight to prepare his next plan even while retreating. And the drive to put that plan into action.*

hunks.sol: On top of that, I had heard his own martial arts were formidable.

hunks.sol: At this point, it almost felt wrong to dismiss him as a mere mounted bandit.

hunks.baseline: It couldn’t be that the Red Wind Band Leader was a Peak master too, could it?
hunks.sol: Surely the Red Wind Band Leader wasn’t a Peak master too… right?

hunks.baseline: I asked Wolhwa just in case.
hunks.sol: I asked Wolhwa just in case, and she immediately nodded.

hunks.baseline: She immediately nodded.
“There has to be a reason someone rose to prominence so quickly. He isn’t widely known yet, but according to our sect’s intelligence, the Red Wind Band Leader is indeed a Peak master.”
hunks.sol: “There’s always a reason someone rises to prominence so quickly. He isn’t widely known yet, but according to our sect’s intelligence, the Red Wind Band Leader is indeed a Peak master.”

hunks.baseline: I was dumbfounded.
hunks.sol: I stared at her in disbelief.

hunks.baseline: “When you meet the Green Forest Alliance Leader or the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League, ask them yourself. Not that you ever will.”
hunks.sol: “If you ever meet the Green Forest Alliance Leader or the Alliance Leader of the Yangtze River Channel League, ask them yourself. Not that you ever will.”

hunks.baseline: “…I sincerely hope that’s true.”
hunks.sol: “…I sincerely hope not.”

hunks.sol: Shaking my head, I mounted one of the horses we had just taken. Jin Mukyung and Hyuk Mujin followed after securely binding the Red Wind Band members and turning them over to the civilians.

hunks.baseline: Deep within the inner grounds of the Mount Heng Sword Sect stood a garden that only a very small number of people were allowed to enter. Cheol Mubaek, the Tiger of Mount Heng, was the only outsider granted that privilege.
hunks.sol: Deep within the inner grounds of the Mount Heng Sword Sect lay a garden that only a select few were permitted to enter. Cheol Mubaek, the Tiger of Mount Heng, was the only outsider ever granted that privilege.

hunks.baseline: “Because it was a special place. Whenever Father had something weighing on his mind, he would come to the garden.”
hunks.sol: “It was a special place. Whenever something weighed on Father’s mind, he would come to the garden.”

hunks.baseline: Lee Seowol walked through the snow-covered garden, her footsteps crunching softly. Then she suddenly stopped when she spotted a frost-covered flower.
hunks.sol: Lee Seowol walked through the snow-covered garden, her footsteps crunching softly. Then she stopped at the sight of a frost-covered flower.

hunks.baseline: “This was one of Mother’s favorite flowers.”
hunks.sol: “Mother loved this flower.”

hunks.baseline: “Was it?”
hunks.sol: “Did she?”

hunks.baseline: “Yes. Whenever she tended the garden, she would always bring me here and tell me the names of the flowers.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Whenever she tended the garden, she would bring me along and teach me the names of the flowers.”

hunks.baseline: After thinking quietly for a moment, Lee Seowol continued.
hunks.sol: Lee Seowol fell silent in thought for a moment before continuing.

hunks.baseline: “But I can’t remember it now.”
hunks.sol: “But I can’t remember its name now.”

hunks.baseline: “It was a long time ago. Don’t trouble yourself over it.”
hunks.sol: “It was a long time ago. Don’t let it trouble you.”

hunks.baseline: “I don’t like flowers. I only followed Mother because she liked them. In truth, I never cared about flowers. It’s the same reason Father used to come to the garden.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t like flowers. I only followed Mother because she did. The truth is, I never cared about them. Father came to this garden for the same reason.”

hunks.baseline: Lee Seowol slowly looked around the snow-covered garden. The flowers had withered, and the number of burial mounds in the center of the garden had grown from one to four.
hunks.sol: Lee Seowol slowly surveyed the snow-covered garden. The flowers had withered, and the burial mounds at its center had grown from one to four.

hunks.baseline: Her gaze sank as she silently stared at the mounds where her family slept.
hunks.sol: Her gaze darkened as she silently stared at the mounds where her family lay.

hunks.baseline: That was why she had lost her father and two older brothers one after another, after losing her mother ten years ago.
hunks.sol: Perhaps that was why, after losing her mother ten years ago, she had lost her father and two older brothers one after another.

hunks.baseline: *I should have kept trying to stop him until the very end…*
hunks.sol: *I should have tried harder to stop him…*

hunks.baseline: A memory from two months ago suddenly resurfaced and blurred her vision.
hunks.sol: A memory from two months ago rose unbidden, blurring her vision.

hunks.baseline: It had been a conversation between father and daughter, held late one night with no one else present.
hunks.sol: It was a conversation between father and daughter, held alone late one night.

hunks.baseline: *“I’ll have to tie you to the third son of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”*
hunks.sol: *“I intend to tie you to the third son of the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”*

hunks.baseline: *“The third son? Surely you’re not thinking of marrying me to that good-for-nothing?”*
hunks.sol: *“The third son? Surely you aren’t thinking of marrying me to that good-for-nothing?”*

hunks.baseline: *“No. But it will become an unbearable scandal for you.”*
hunks.sol: *“No. But it will cause a scandal you may find difficult to endure.”*

hunks.baseline: *“What can I do? It’s my fault for having a heartless father.”*
hunks.sol: *“What else can I do? It’s my fault for having a heartless father.”*

hunks.baseline: *“You’re a child I can never understand. Are you really all right with this?”*
hunks.sol: *“I can never make sense of you. Does this truly not bother you?”*

hunks.baseline: *“If I say I don’t like it, will you change your mind?”*
hunks.sol: *“If I said I didn’t want this, would you change your mind?”*

hunks.baseline: *“At the very least, I’ll look for another way.”*
hunks.sol: *“At the very least, I would look for another way.”*

hunks.baseline: *“So the war with the Jin Family of Taiyuan is a foregone conclusion.”*
hunks.sol: *“So war with the Jin Family of Taiyuan is already a foregone conclusion.”*

hunks.baseline: *“Now that the Strange Hero of Shanxi and the Heaven Shaking Sword are absent, this is the perfect time. This opportunity will never come again.”*
hunks.sol: *“Now is the perfect time, with the Strange Hero of Shanxi and the Heaven Shaking Sword both absent. An opportunity like this will never come again.”*

hunks.baseline: *“No. My decision has already been made.”*
hunks.sol: *“Impossible. My decision has already been made.”*

hunks.baseline: *“Then make sure you win. Become strong enough that no one in Shanxi can even open their mouth about a scandal involving me.”*
hunks.sol: *“Then make certain you win. Become so powerful that no one in Shanxi would dare breathe a word about any scandal involving me.”*

hunks.baseline: *“…If you had been a man, I would have made you the Young Sect Leader.”*
hunks.sol: *“…Had you been born a man, I would have made you the Young Sect Leader.”*

hunks.baseline: *“I’m glad I was born a woman. I have no interest in being this sect’s Young Sect Leader.”*
hunks.sol: *“Then I’m glad I was born a woman. I have no interest in becoming the Young Sect Leader of this sect.”*

hunks.baseline: Had even a fortnight passed before Lee Seogeun returned as a cold corpse? Not long after, she lost Lee Cheonbaek, and in the end, even her eldest older brother, Lee Seogwang.
hunks.sol: Had even a fortnight passed before Lee Seogeun returned as a cold corpse? Not long after, she lost Lee Cheonbaek. In the end, even her eldest brother, Lee Seogwang, was gone.

hunks.baseline: *Now I’m alone.*
hunks.sol: *Now I’m all alone.*

hunks.sol: And so, Lee Seowol, the last surviving blood relative of the Blood Wolf Sword Lee Cheonbaek, became the new Sect Leader.
